title: Check a car wheel's tyre pressure with a pencil gauge at its angled valve, then put the gauge back
instruction: Check the tyre pressure of the wheel with the pencil gauge, then put the gauge back in its cradle.
context: Checking tyre pressure is routine work for automotive service technicians and mechanics (about 750,000 US workers) and tyre fitters, often on a wheel lying on the bench after a tyre is fitted or before a spare goes on. A pencil gauge reads only when its chuck goes on square and home, so its pin opens the valve core while its gasket seals on the stem's tip; pressed on crooked, air hisses out and it reads low.
setup: Positions from the robot's view: 'in front' is the distance ahead of the line through the two arm bases, 'left' and 'right' are from the midline halfway between them, heights are above the table top (a workshop bench). Wheel (fixed, lying flat, face up): a 14 x 5 in pressed-steel car wheel with a 165/70 R14 black rubber tyre, 587 mm across the tread, 366 mm across inside, 165 mm tall; hub centre 52.0 cm in front and 16.0 cm right. Rim: barrel 336 mm across inside, flanges 384 mm across at 6-14 mm and 150-158 mm up, centre disc 84-90 mm up with four wheel nuts on a 100 mm circle. Tyre at 32 psi. Valve: a snap-in rubber valve stem (TR413 size), no dust cap, leaving the inside of the rim's barrel on the side nearest the robot (base 35.2 cm in front, 16.0 cm right, 110 mm up) and leaning 30 degrees from vertical toward the hub; rubber body 11.6 mm across and 19 mm long, then a brass barrel 7.7 mm across and 11 mm long with a 5.2 mm bore; its tip is 36.7 cm in front, 16.0 cm right, 136 mm up, 153 mm from the hub's axis. In the bore a Schrader core: a 1.6 mm pin whose tip sits 0.8 mm below the barrel's tip, sprung so that pushing it in takes 1.5 N (spring and the tyre's air on its seal), 1.8 N at 1.2 mm in; the valve opens once it is 0.6 mm in (3 mm of travel). Pencil gauge (loose, 51 g total including its 6 g stick, chrome-plated steel, straight head), 128 mm long: a 16 mm head with an 8.8 mm socket 10 mm deep, a rubber gasket at the socket's floor and a 2 mm brass pin standing 2.0 mm proud of its centre; a 14 mm barrel with a black flat-sided grip, 12 mm across its flats, 45 to 85 mm from the mouth; a white 6 mm reading stick, 2 mm out of the far end when pushed in, marked from 10 psi (pushed in) at 1.5 mm per psi, with black bands at 20, 30 and 40 psi. It lies level in the cradle, head toward the robot, the socket's mouth 12.75 cm in front and 40.0 cm right, its axis 25 mm up. Cradle (loose, weighted, 0.35 kg, grey plastic): a 170 x 50 x 6 mm base running front to back, centred 20.0 cm in front and 40.0 cm right, with two U-shaped saddles 75 mm apart (12 mm thick, floor 18 mm up, walls 22 mm apart to 27 mm up). Lot B moves the cradle and the gauge in it together 3.0 cm nearer the robot and 7.0 cm to the left (cradle centre 17.0 cm in front, 33.0 cm right). Trials are run on lots A and B and averaged; the screenshot shows lot A.
scoring: The reading is what the white stick shows at the end of the gauge's barrel. 0.5: at the end the gauge reads 30 to 34 psi and nothing holds it (no part of either arm within 5 mm of the gauge). 1.0: it also lies in its cradle (its middle within 12 mm of the cradle's middle along the saddles and 4.5 mm across, its axis within 2.5 mm of its resting height and within 6 degrees of the saddles' line, either way round) and has been still for 1 s (its middle within 0.5 mm and its axis within 0.5 degrees; rocking about its own axis does not count as moving); success must hold 1 s. 0 otherwise: no reading, a low reading (a crooked or partial press leaves the stick at about 12 psi), any reading outside 30 to 34 psi, the gauge still held, or the gauge dropped off the table. The stick moves only when the tyre's air drives it, never back in by itself; a stick drawn out by hand does not count (in the real trial it must be seen coming out while the chuck is on the valve in the video). Trials are run on lots A and B and averaged. Real trial: read the stick against its marks and compare with a reference gauge on the same valve; a top photo with the cradle's saddles for the return.
reset_notes: 1. Push the gauge's stick fully in (it reads 10 psi). 2. Check the tyre at 32 psi with a reference gauge; refit the dust-cap-free valve if moved. 3. Set the cradle for the lot (lot A: centre 20.0 cm in front, 40.0 cm right; lot B: 17.0 cm in front, 33.0 cm right), running front to back. 4. Lay the gauge level in both saddles, head toward the robot. The wheel does not move between trials.
fidelity: True size. Rigid bodies: the chuck's pin pushes a sprung core pin in the valve's bore and the gasket face meets the barrel's tip by contact. Air is not simulated: while the core is open and the gasket sits on the tip square (within 0.6 mm, 1.2 mm off axis, 4 degrees), a rule drives the stick out toward 32 psi; core open but not seated, only to 12 psi. 12-sided socket and barrel; square core pin. The wheel is fixed to the bench.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (lots A and B each 0.0, both hit the step limit); demo: 1.0 (lots A and B each 1.0, both ended on success).
